note: Per-gate cardinality contract consumed by GgenIgniter.GateVerify.run/3 (:cardinality opt)
and by `mix ggen_igniter.verify`. Keyed by GATE STEM -- the name
GgenIgniter.Pack.discover_queries/1 derives by stripping the NNN_ prefix from
gates/NNN_stem.rq -- NOT by filename.
WHY THIS EXISTS, alongside the inverted verify/*.unbound.rq queries: those queries name a
missing PREDICATE on an individual, but a contract catches a DROP the queries cannot model.
The two are complementary only when their blind spots differ, which is what the anchor
choice below is for.
MODE is load-bearing, not decoration. A simpler design -- compare a gate's DISTINCT first
column against a count of individuals -- produces a FALSE POSITIVE on `attributes`, because
gates/040_attributes.rq projects ?resource_module first, not an attribute identity: its
first column has 2 distinct values while 9 attribute individuals exist. None of the gates
selects a subject IRI at all, so no fully automatic derivation is available and the mode
has to be declared.
ROWS   -- the gate emits exactly one row per anchored subject.
VALUES -- the gate emits exactly one row per (subject, value) pair; for a repeatable
property such as amp:defaultAction or amp:refusalReason.
ANCHOR: exactly one of `predicate` (preferred) or `class`. A contract compares a gate row
count against a count derived from the SAME graph, so it is structurally blind to any
deletion that moves both numbers together -- the loss of its own anchor. That makes the
anchor a real choice, and it was made from measurement, not taste. Deleting a Resource's
rdf:type from this ontology drops gates/030_resources.rq from 2 rows to 1; a CLASS-anchored
contract also drops 2 -> 1 and sees nothing, and verify/030_resources.unbound.rq is blind
too because it anchors on `?subject a amp:Resource` as well -- one shared blind spot, one
uncovered defect. A PREDICATE-anchored contract reports gate 1 vs contract 2 and CATCHES
it, and its own blind spot (loss of the anchor predicate itself) is exactly what the
inverted companion names. Disjoint blind spots, so every contract below is
predicate-anchored. The class anchor stays supported for a gate whose anchor predicate is
shared across classes; it is a weaker default, not a wrong one.
MEASURED, not assumed. Every contract below was run against
test/fixtures/ash_manufacture_pack/ontology.ttl through GgenIgniter.Query.run/2 (the
`sparql` hex engine GateVerify itself uses) and matched its gate exactly: project 1==1,
domains 2==2, resources 2==2, default_actions 8==8, attributes 9==9, relationships 1==1,
extensions 2==2, support_modules 5==5, enum_values 3==3, capabilities 21==21,
refusals 9==9.
The counts themselves are deliberately NOT written down here. A contract is a relation
between the graph and the gate, so it stays correct as the ontology grows; a hardcoded
number would go stale on the next resource added and become a second source of truth.
`refusals` is a filtered gate (gates/085_refusals.rq matches `amp:admitted false`), so any
class-wide count would be wrong -- 21 capabilities, 9 rows. Anchoring on amp:refusalReason
is exact instead, for a MEASURED reason rather than an assumed one: zero admitted
capabilities carry an amp:refusalReason in this ontology (`SELECT ?s WHERE { ?s a
amp:GeneratorCapability ; amp:admitted true ; amp:refusalReason ?r }` returns 0 rows), so
'carries a refusalReason' and 'is inadmissible' are the same set. If a future edit gives an
admitted capability a refusal reason this contract fires, which is correct -- that
combination is itself a modelling defect.
ADDITIVE BY CONSTRUCTION: a gate stem absent from `gates` below keeps GateVerify's
documented default (a gate passes on >= 1 row). Other packs in this repo were authored
against that rule and ship no cardinality.json at all. `citations` and `dependency_pins`
are intentionally absent here and run under that default.
